display-small.purpose: The one heading of each centered screen: start, progress, done, empty, error.

title-large.purpose: The side-sheet title and the editable name of a folder, the dialog title, the app-bar wordmark.

title-medium.purpose: The source node's name, the counts of top-level cards with tabular figures, the large button's label.

title-small.purpose: Folder and subfolder card names, subfolder card counts, the add-folder label, segmented-button labels, the names in the sheet's Subfolders rows, the busy strip's title.

body-large.purpose: Lead paragraph under a screen heading (44ch max); the dialog's name field and Location select.

body-medium.purpose: Base size: sheet rows, menu items, assist chips, the snackbar's message, Settings rows, the trust line.

body-small.purpose: Hints, the privacy note, the bookmarks-bar label, the backup note, the sheet's path line and Display label, supporting lines of start-screen rows, dialog choices and banners; node meta lines, the host and reason lines of sheet rows and a root label's drop hint use the size without tracking.

label-large.purpose: Button labels, the snackbar's Undo included.

label-medium.purpose: Menu headers and the root labels inside move menus, Settings group headings, the root labels of the destination column, the sheet's Subfolders label, the Location field label, the suggestion chips.

shadows.name: elev-1
shadows.purpose: Hover on filled buttons, folder and subfolder cards, the sheet's folder tile, the suggestion chips and the File all as suggested chip; the notice banner at rest.

shadows.name: elev-2
shadows.purpose: Menus and the emoji picker; the card under a dragged bookmark or folder.

shadows.name: elev-3
shadows.purpose: The dialog; the side sheet when it overlays the board below 1024px; the snackbar.

shadows.name: selection-ring
shadows.purpose: Open card, folder or subfolder, over a 1px primary border, drawn around the whole card with its fold chevron.

shadows.name: drop-target
shadows.purpose: Card under the pointer while a bookmark or a folder is dragged, with a 10% teal wash.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Every focusable element; offset -3px inside the segmented button.

shadows.name: favicon-ring
shadows.purpose: Cut-out ring separating overlapping favicons; --ring is the card color.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: State layers (150ms), the disclosure and fold chevron turns (200ms), progress width (250ms), indeterminate progress slide (1.4s loop).

motion.name: ease-emphasized
motion.purpose: Connector draw-in, side-sheet entrance, snackbar entrance, switch thumb.

motion.name: state-layer
motion.purpose: Hover and pressed overlays (8% and 12%), node border, background, opacity and shadow changes, root-label edges during a drag, connector color.

motion.name: connector-draw
motion.purpose: Connectors draw in once per proposal; the dotted Duplicates and Removed lines fade in; redraws after edits, folds or resizes are instant.

motion.name: sheet-enter
motion.purpose: Side sheet slides 24px in from the inline end (the right, the left in Arabic) while fading in.

motion.name: snackbar-enter
motion.purpose: The snackbar rises 8px and fades in on the emphasized curve.

motion.name: snackbar-dwell
motion.purpose: The snackbar leaves after 8s, never during a drag or with a menu or dialog open (it checks again every 2s).

motion.name: switch-thumb
motion.purpose: Thumb travels from 6px to 22px and grows from 16px to 24px.

motion.name: fold-chevron
motion.purpose: Folding a folder turns its chevron -90° (90° in Arabic) on the standard curve.

motion.name: progress-indeterminate
motion.purpose: A 40% segment slides across the track, the other way in Arabic.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Animations and transitions drop to 1ms; connectors appear drawn, the sheet and the snackbar appear in place; indeterminate progress becomes a static full bar at 40% opacity.

breakpoints.name: stacked
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: edge-to-edge workspace, single stacked column, no connectors or ports (the folder tree keeps its rails), static source node, style switch leaves the app bar, trust line on its own row, the undo icon button leaves the toolbar and its buttons wrap to the end edge; start-screen segmented buttons take the full row and drop their check.

breakpoints.name: sheet-overlay
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: the side sheet overlays the board under the app bar at min(400px, 100vw) with elev-3.

breakpoints.name: sheet-docked
breakpoints.purpose: From here up: the side sheet docks as a 400px column.

breakpoints.name: strip-hint
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: the bookmarks-bar hint is hidden.

breakpoints.name: dests-two-favicons
breakpoints.purpose: Destination column at or below: favicon preview drops from three to two.

breakpoints.name: dests-no-favicons
breakpoints.purpose: Destination column at or below: favicon preview disappears before names truncate.

components.name: Filled Button
components.description: The one primary action of a screen or dialog (Analyze, File the bookmarks, Finish, Create, Discard, Delete, Retry), with a leading 18px symbol; on the review board it carries the number of bookmarks it files.

components.name: Text Button

components.name: Outlined Text Field and Select
components.description: The new-folder dialog's fields: the name field, then the Location select drawn as the same outlined field and labelled in label medium; 56px, 4px corners, a 1px outline edge that thickens to 2px teal on focus without moving the text. Options show depth with em-space indents, since native options cannot be styled.
components.css: .ds-fields { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 16px; width: 312px; } .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; } .ds-field input, .ds-field select { box-sizing: border-box; height: 56px; border: 1px solid var(--outline, #6f7977); border-radius: 4px; background: transparent; color: var(--on-surface, #171d1c); font: 400 1rem/1.5rem var(--font, 'Google Sans', system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-field input { padding: 0 16px; } .ds-field select { padding: 0 12px; } .ds-field input:focus { outline: none; border: 2px solid var(--primary, #006a62); padding: 0 15px; } .ds-field select:focus { outline: none; border: 2px solid var(--primary, #006a62); padding: 0 11px; } .ds-field-label { padding: 0 4px; color: var(--on-surface-variant, #3f4947); font: 500 0.75rem/1rem var(--font, 'Google Sans', system-ui, sans-serif); }

components.name: Bookmarks-bar Chips
components.description: The strip above the canvas previews the new bar: quick-access chips first (icon only by default, the pressed state), one with its name shown, then the folders created in the bar as chips with the emoji Chrome will show; a click on a folder chip opens that folder in the side sheet. Favicons are stand-ins.

New bar

components.name: Folder Tree During a Drag
components.description: The destination column while a bookmark from the open subfolder Home automation is dragged: the root labels lit as drop zones with their hint, lit cards with filled ports, the open subfolder faded under its selection ring, Recipes as the drop target under the pointer, Tech folded, then Not recreated with Duplicates (never a target, faded) and Removed (lit), and the dashed add-folder slot. Subfolders are 44px cards hanging from their folder on 1px rails; hover a root label to see it take the drop. Favicons are stand-ins.

A fixed left-to-right diagram.

components.name: Docked Action Bar and Snackbar
components.description: The last row of the review board: the trust line at the start; at the end the undo icon button (once there is an edit to undo), the Restore proposal text button and the filled Apply button with the number of bookmarks it files. Above it, the snackbar of the last edit, anchored 12px over the bar and centered: inverse surface, an inverse-primary Undo, a close button, Level 3, rising in over 200ms.

narrative.overview:
Nidomark's screens read like the plan a mover draws before the truck arrives: every bookmark is shown on its way to a labelled folder of the new tree, line weights say how much travels where, and nothing leaves its shelf until the user signs at the bottom of the page. The visual language is Google's Material 3 taken at face value (tonal color roles, Google Sans, Material Symbols Rounded, pill-shaped buttons, a three-step soft elevation scale), so the extension feels like part of Chrome rather than a guest in it, light or dark as the browser decides.

The personality is spent in one place, the review canvas: a single source card on a dotted floor, curves fanning out to a column of folder cards, each curve as heavy as the number of bookmarks it carries, drawn in once when the proposal arrives, and subfolders hanging under their folder on thin rails like the branches of the plan. Around it the chrome stays quiet at a comfortable Material density (40px controls, 56px folder cards, 44px subfolder cards, 64px sheet rows), with one teal for acting and choosing and one amber for whatever deserves a second look.

Reassurance is part of the visual system rather than a message: the toolbar docked under the canvas says that nothing has changed yet at every width, the Apply button states how many bookmarks it will file, an edit answers in a snackbar that offers to undo it, and the start screen says, right above the Analyze button, that the current tree is kept in a dated backup. The analysis progress screen follows the same tokens; it is recorded here from code and has no reference screenshot yet.
keyCharacteristics: Material 3 color roles with a light and a dark value each, switched by prefers-color-scheme.
Tonal layering builds the structure; shadows appear only as a response or for overlays.
One family, Google Sans, in two weights (400 and 500) on the Material type scale.
Pill buttons, 16px cards and nodes, 12px tiles and subfolder cards, 8px chips.
A node canvas whose connector weight encodes bookmark counts; subfolders hang from their folder on 1px rails.
Drag and drop of bookmarks and folders with lit targets, always paired with a menu path.
Every edit reported in a snackbar with Undo.
Logical properties throughout, so the page mirrors in Arabic.

rules.name: The Two Signals Rule
rules.body: Teal says act, choose or focus; amber says look again (To check, suggestions, caution). No other hue belongs to the interface: folder emoji and site favicons are content, not palette.

rules.name: The Raised Node Rule
rules.body: A node always sits one tonal step above the canvas: white over the mist floor in light, surface-high over the near-black floor in dark. Never fill a node with the canvas color, and never with surface-lowest in dark.

rules.name: The Seam and Edge Rule
rules.body: Seams between sections and between list rows are 1px surface-high. Stronger edges belong to objects: outline-variant around nodes and chips, outline around outlined controls, fields and the switch. The rails of the folder tree take the node edge, 1px outline-variant, so a subfolder reads as hanging from its folder.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: Regular (400) for reading and for headings, Medium (500) for names, counts and actions. Headings grow in size, not in weight.

rules.name: The Names Before Pictures Rule
rules.body: When the destinations column narrows, the favicon preview gives up room first: three icons, then two below a 400px column, then none below 340px. A folder name may truncate only after that.

rules.name: The Docked Toolbar Rule
rules.body: The apply toolbar is the last row of the board, never a bar floating over the canvas. Its trust line stays visible at every width, and the Apply button carries the number of bookmarks it files. The snackbar is the one thing that floats, 12px above it, and it leaves on its own.

rules.name: The Lift Is a Response Rule
rules.body: Nodes, list cards, the workspace and the docked sheet are flat at rest; a shadow appears because the pointer is there, a menu opened, a drop is possible, or a layer floats over the board (the dialog, the overlaid sheet, the snackbar).

rules.name: The Pill Is for Buttons Rule
rules.body: Only buttons and switches are pills. Nodes and chips are clickable too, but keep rectangular corners so they read as objects rather than commands; the sheet's assist chips act, yet keep the chip's 8px corners.

rules.name: The Dashed Means Not Yet Rule
rules.body: A dashed stroke marks an empty slot or a bookmark that is not recreated: the add-folder node, the empty-folder drop zone, the root labels while a drag is on (an open slot at the top of a root), the dotted Duplicates and Removed connectors (1px dash, 5px gap). It never decorates a filled container.

rules.name: The One Filled Button Rule
rules.body: A screen or dialog has at most one filled button; every other action is tonal, outlined or text.

rules.name: The Weight Is Data Rule
rules.body: A connector's stroke is 1.5px plus 0.5px per bookmark it carries, subfolders included, capped at twelve bookmarks (7.5px). The Duplicates and Removed connectors are always 1.5px and dotted.

rules.name: The Draw Once Rule
rules.body: Connectors draw in once per proposal (700ms on the emphasized curve, 40ms stagger per folder, the dotted lines fading in); later redraws after an edit, a fold or a resize happen without motion.

dos: Do take every color from the role tokens, and give any new surface both its light and its -dark value.
Do keep teal for actions, selection, focus and progress, and amber for To check, suggestions and caution (The Two Signals Rule).
Do fill nodes with node, which resolves to surface-high in dark, so they stay raised over the canvas (The Raised Node Rule).
Do keep the apply toolbar docked as the board's last row, with the trust line visible at every width and the bookmark count on the Apply button.
Do let connector weight carry the count (1.5px plus 0.5px per bookmark, 7.5px at most) and draw connectors in only once per proposal.
Do hang subfolders under their folder as 44px cards on 1px outline-variant rails, and keep connectors for the top-level cards.
Do shrink the favicon preview (three, two, none) before a folder name may truncate.

Do pair every drag gesture, of a bookmark or of a folder, with a menu path (the row menu, the folder's Move chip), light only the cards and root labels that can accept the drop, and fade the other cards to 55%.
Do report each edit in the snackbar above the toolbar, with its Undo, and keep Ctrl+Z working outside text fields.
Do write every directional value as a logical property, so the page mirrors in Arabic.
Do honor reduced motion: connectors, the sheet and the snackbar appear without animation, and unknown progress becomes a static bar.
Do set text in Google Sans at 400 or 500 on the Material type scale.

Do draw icons as inline Material Symbols Rounded SVG: 24px by default, 18px in buttons, chips, segments, subfolder tiles and fold chevrons, 16px in the compact segmented button, 20px for the trust line's info icon.
donts: Don't float the apply toolbar over the canvas or move the bookmark count out of the Apply button.
Don't use teal or amber as decoration; apart from the Settings group headings and status line, teal text is always something to press or, during a drag, a place to drop.
Don't lift resting nodes, list cards, the workspace or the docked sheet with a shadow; the notice banner is the one elevated card.
Don't put emoji or Unicode symbols in place of Material Symbols for interface actions and states; emoji belong to folder names.
Don't hide the trust line at any width.
Don't draw connectors or ports in the stacked layout at 760px and below.
Don't run a connector to a subfolder card or give it a port; its rail ties it to its folder.
Don't replay the connector animation after the first draw.
